answer: In a walled market garden, each grower keeps one falcon to guard the beds from pigeons. The falcon wears a thread band registered to its handler, and the garden keeper logs every flight with the date and the pigeons driven off. Twice a month the keeper checks the band against the register and watches the bird fly, and a handler caught flying a second bird under the same name loses the plot for the season. To fake a thousand names, an attacker must train a thousand falcons, fly each one on its rota, and pass a thousand band checks that all match.
